tasks.short: Arrange and evidence delivery of legal correspondence.

steps.what: Receive approved correspondence, recipient details and dispatch instructions.
Confirm required delivery method, recipients and any procedural service deadline.
Assemble attachments, covering correspondence, delivery labels and enclosure lists.
Check document versions, recipients, enclosures and addresses before authorising release.
Send electronic correspondence through the authorised channel.
Print, seal and hand physical packs to the approved delivery provider.
Record delivery evidence and chase failed or unconfirmed deliveries.

tasks.design: A structured dispatch request in {WORKFLOW} pulls approved documents from {DOCS}, validates recipient fields and generates the dispatch pack. One recorded release approval binds the document versions, recipients and route; supported electronic channels execute that approval and return receipts to the legal matter-management category in {OTHER}. Physical dispatch and exceptional service arrangements stay with people, while failed-delivery alerts are automated.
tasks.previous_blocker: The pack, recipient list, procedural instruction and delivery evidence lived in separate places. A wrong attachment or delivery route made unattended dispatch unattractive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval flows, document references and delivery-status interfaces can connect the process. A small deterministic pack generator removes repeated assembly without requiring a model.
tasks.still_hard: A delivery receipt does not necessarily prove legally valid service. National procedural rules, unavailable portal interfaces, physical originals and disputed receipt still require attention.
tasks.human_edge: Checking whether delivery is appropriate in the matter's context and handling sensitive recipients or failed formal service.

ambition.what: A delivery-evidence register for time-critical legal correspondence.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time assembling packs and chasing routine receipts. They gain delegated authority to resolve ordinary address and delivery failures within approved routes; procedural exceptions return to the matter lawyer.

reach.task: Maintain traceable handovers for tracked physical correspondence.
reach.learn: Chain of custody, receipt matching and the distinction between delivery tracking and legal service.

evidence.claim: Template assembly, release approvals and receipt matching can use deterministic rules; the proposed gains are estimates.
Valid service and acceptable delivery channels depend on the procedure and national rules.

assumptions: Shares represent a mixed workload of electronic and physical dispatch; these are alternative routes for individual items.
Electronic automation covers channels with approved sending interfaces; unsupported portals require manual dispatch.
The release approval in s4 is reused by s5 or s6, without a second routine approval.
The legal matter-management category is represented by {OTHER}.
GDPR applies to recipient and matter data; national rules govern formal service requirements.
No employee monitoring is introduced; consultation needs must still be checked under national rules.
Build ranges estimate working effort and exclude external delivery-provider lead times.
unknowns: Which delivery channels are legally accepted for the team's matters.
Whether supported electronic dispatch interfaces and reliable receipts are available.
The proportion of physical correspondence and formal-service cases.
Who has delegated release authority and which correspondence requires lawyer approval.
Applicable employee consultation and access-approval requirements.
research_questions: Which channel interfaces preserve document identity, timestamps and recipient evidence?
How should each procedural route distinguish transmission, delivery and valid service?
new_work: Maintain approved delivery routes and recipient validation rules.
Review release packs and failed-delivery exceptions.
Reconcile missing receipts and duplicate dispatch attempts.
Invalidate approval whenever a document, recipient or route changes.
tasks.statement: Mail, fax, or arrange for delivery of legal correspondence to clients, witnesses, and court officials.

tasks.short: Receive, place and route legal-team telephone calls.

steps.what: Greet the caller or confirm the intended recipient of an outbound call.
Clarify the purpose, urgency and disclosure limits of the call.
Find permitted matter details, the responsible colleague and their availability.
Give authorised administrative information, connect the call or agree a callback.
Write a call note with contact details and agreed follow-up.
Send the responsible colleague the call note or callback request.

tasks.design: Connect the {TELEPHONY} to a restricted lookup panel showing permitted context from the {DOCS} and availability from the {CALENDAR}. Configure a short call-note form in the {WORKFLOW} to reuse contact details and notify the responsible colleague through the {EMAIL}; the legal assistant conducts the conversation and enters its outcome.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fragmented directories, matter permissions and availability made preparation slow. The conversation itself was never the main technical gap.
tasks.enabler_now: Small deterministic integrations and configured forms can remove lookup and routing work at modest cost.
tasks.still_hard: Identity checks, distressed callers, negotiation and deciding what may be disclosed still need a person.
tasks.human_edge: Building trust, noticing hesitation or urgency and avoiding disclosure before authority is clear.

ambition.what: A tracked callback commitment with an agreed owner and due time.

tasks.altitude: The legal assistant spends less time searching and forwarding messages, with more attention available during calls. They can agree callbacks within delegated service limits; legal advice and disclosure authority do not expand.

reach.task: Coordinate sensitive callbacks for senior staff.
reach.learn: Escalation thresholds, delegated commitments and confidential message handling.

evidence.claim: Permission-aware lookup, structured call notes and callback routing can use deterministic technology.
The proposed time reductions and build ranges are estimates; the digest provides no legal-call automation case.
In the Netherlands, lawyer secrecy obligations also cover employees and staff.
The EU AI Act treats some staff allocation and monitoring uses separately from ordinary administrative assistance.

assumptions: Calls remain human, without recording, transcription or a voice bot.
Lookup results do not establish caller identity or authorise disclosure.
Notifications contain minimal details and a permission-controlled link to the call note.
Substantive legal questions go to legal counsel.
No staff performance monitoring or automated workload allocation is included.
unknowns: Can the {TELEPHONY} expose call events and support an authorised lookup integration?
Where are matter ownership and disclosure permissions recorded?
What identity checks and escalation rules already apply?
Which callback commitments may the legal assistant make?
Would the integration require consultation under applicable national rules?

Which call types cause the most searching, transfers or missed callbacks?

Resolve unmatched callers and failed notifications.
Review overdue callback commitments.
Check that lookup permissions remain aligned with matter access.

tasks.short: Arrange appointments for lawyers, checking availability, urgency and confidentiality.

steps.what: Read the appointment request and clarify participants, purpose, duration and constraints.
Check calendars, travel buffers and room availability for suitable slots.
Exchange proposed times and resolve clashes, urgency or sensitive attendance.
Create the appointment and send invitations with appropriate visibility and meeting details.
Check acceptances and chase missing confirmations.

tasks.design: Configure structured requests, availability rules, booking links and neutral reminders in the {WORKFLOW} and {CALENDAR}. The legal assistant resolves difficult clashes and checks recipients and visibility before invitations leave the {CALENDAR}; acceptance tracking removes routine chasing through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrived in different formats, and booking rules were implicit. External availability and sensitive participant lists still required coordination.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing booking features cover routine coordination. AI-assisted coding can make small adapters and request forms cheaper to build where configuration falls short.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent legal appointments, external calendars and confidential attendance require context. Court-fixed dates cannot be moved through ordinary booking rules.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising which clash merits interrupting a lawyer and negotiating without exposing confidential information.

ambition.what: Self-service appointment requests for regional office staff

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward urgent clashes and preparation gaps. With delegated authority, the assistant can release routine appointments within agreed scheduling priorities; lawyers retain substantive priority decisions.

reach.task: Coordinate shared executive and legal meeting availability
reach.learn: Calendar delegation, travel buffers and escalation priorities

evidence.claim: Existing calendar booking rules and reminders can handle routine appointments without a model.
Microsoft 365 Copilot can turn an email thread into an invitation with an agenda.
The UK department evaluation reported scheduling taking longer on average; automation needs a local comparison.
EU AI Act requirements depend on use; routine scheduling differs from allocating tasks or monitoring staff.

assumptions: The setting is an internal legal team in a company with 200 to 2,000 staff.
Structured intake covers routine requests; unusual requests remain with the assistant.
Routine reminders contain neutral appointment details and follow agreed rules.
The coordination prior is useful, but this reconstruction places more work in the mailbox than its weak mail estimate.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Access work includes GDPR review and employee consultation where national rules apply.

How many appointments involve court-fixed dates or confidential participant lists
Whether national rules require consultation for changed calendar access

Which invitation fields need a human check to prevent confidentiality errors?
Does structured intake reduce clarification without discouraging urgent requests?
new_work: Maintain appointment types, buffers and visibility rules.
Handle booking failures and unresolved clashes.
Review invitation recipients and confidential details.
Check reminder effectiveness and excessive notifications.

tasks.short: Make and distribute copies of legal correspondence and documents.

steps.what: Confirm the required documents, recipients, copy counts and paper requirements.
Find the approved originals in the matter file or paper folder.
Photocopy originals using office copying equipment.
Check readability, page order, missing pages and unintended confidential attachments.
Hand the checked pack to the requesting colleague.

tasks.design: Configure a copy-request form in the {WORKFLOW} and retrieve approved versions from the {DOCS}, replacing paper copies with permission-controlled digital packs where accepted. A deterministic pack builder checks page counts and order before review; secure print presets on the {OTHER} office copying equipment support the remaining paper work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper habits, uncertain recipient requirements and inconsistent document versions mattered more than missing technology.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document permissions, secure printing and inexpensive pack-building code can remove much handling without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Bound originals, damaged pages, certified copies and mandatory paper delivery still require physical work.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when the wrong version, recipient or attachment could compromise a matter.
tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer copying trips and more time resolving document exceptions. No new legal decision rights follow.

reach.learn: Version control, document permissions and requirements for physical originals.

evidence.claim: Digital substitution, secure printing and deterministic pack assembly are established approaches; these time estimates are hypotheses.
Dutch legal-profession guidance requires protecting confidential information when using AI tools.

assumptions: This is internal legal support in a mid-size European company.
Most requested originals already exist digitally in the {DOCS}; paper-only files are exceptions.
Enough recipients accept digital packs to reduce physical handling.
The delivery step covers internal distribution; external disclosure requires separate authority.
Build ranges cover one document repository and existing office equipment.
unknowns: Which recipients require paper, certification or original documents?
How much copying starts from paper-only originals?
Are document permissions and approved versions reliable?
Do existing equipment and employment arrangements require consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Which paper requirements are binding, and which are local habits?
Can existing configuration provide digital packs and secure release printing?
new_work: Maintain copy-request defaults and pack specifications.
Review flagged page and attachment exceptions.
Maintain document access and secure printing configuration.
tasks.statement: Make photocopies of correspondence, documents, and other printed matter.

tasks.short: Maintain legal case files, document indexes and reference libraries.

steps.what: Collect incoming correspondence, case documents, receipts and library updates.
Read documents and assign matter identifiers, document types and reference metadata.

loop.input: Unmatched documents, permitted matter identifiers and the filing taxonomy.
loop.output: Proposed matter, document type and metadata with supporting text locations.
loop.check: Validate identifiers against matter records; require source support and assistant approval for inferred classifications.
loop.stop: One classification attempt per document; ambiguous, conflicting or unreadable documents enter the manual queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use existing identifiers and routing rules first. Unlabelled correspondence still needs free-text interpretation.

steps.what: Save documents in the matter-management system and maintain versions in the document store.
Copy document references into the team's separate matter index.
Decide access exceptions, retention changes and legal holds referred by the assistant.
Check library holdings, superseded guidance and missing reference material.

tasks.design: Connect approved intake channels to the legal matter-management category in {OTHER} and versioned storage in {DOCS}; replace the separate {SPREADSHEET} index with saved views. Route documents by identifiers first, then use one bounded classification pass for unmatched material, with assistant approval of inferred metadata. Configure permissions and retention alerts in {DOCS}; access exceptions, hold changes and disposal decisions stay with the authorised person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Matter identifiers, document versions and mailbox attachments were disconnected. Maintaining custom connectors and a filing taxonomy cost more than repeated manual filing.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records features handle versions and permissions. AI-assisted coding lowers connector costs, while bounded text classification can propose metadata for unlabelled documents.
tasks.still_hard: Incorrect matter assignment can expose confidential information. Privilege, retention and legal holds depend on the matter and national rules; current legal authority still needs human verification.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising sensitive context, distinguishing legal significance from filing convenience, and knowing when a reference is no longer reliable.

ambition.what: Permission-controlled matter-document retrieval for project managers.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time copying and locating files and more time resolving ambiguous records. They gain delegated authority to correct metadata and duplicates, while legal access and retention decisions remain with authorised roles.

reach.task: Maintain a shared records taxonomy and resolve duplicate records.
reach.learn: Version control, retention categories, access inheritance and reversible record corrections.

evidence.claim: BaseNeQXt provides legal case files, conflict checks, templates, time registration and invoicing.
The proposed routing, review shares and implementation ranges are design estimates, not documented savings.
Dutch professional guidance recommends protecting confidential data and manually verifying legal citations.

Maintain routing rules, taxonomy mappings and connector credentials.
Check failed imports, version conflicts and access inheritance.
Review retention alerts without automatically deleting held records.
tasks.statement: Organize and maintain law libraries, documents, and case files.

tasks.short: Collect employment, medical and other records for legal matters.

steps.what: Define which records the matter needs and why.
Check existing records, request authority, recipient details and required permissions.
Prepare and send scoped record requests with the required authority.
Track outstanding requests and send routine reminders.
Register received records, check identity and dates, and index their contents.

loop.input: Received records and the approved record scope.
loop.output: Proposed record index with identity, dates, document types and page references.
loop.check: Validate field formats and requested date coverage; link every extracted value to a page. A person verifies identity and ambiguous fields before accepting the index.
loop.stop: One extraction pass per document and one validation retry; unreadable or conflicting records enter a manual queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: External records use varied layouts and free text. Existing metadata is reused without a model where sufficient.

steps.what: Review gaps and decide whether further records are legally necessary.

tasks.design: Use a restricted request register in the {WORKFLOW}, linked to the {DOCS}, to generate scoped requests, track receipts and send approved reminders through the {EMAIL}. A bounded extraction loop proposes a source-linked record index, while deterministic checks expose missing dates and documents for legal counsel's decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Record holders use different formats and response channels, while authority and completeness depend on the matter.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic request tracking can be built cheaply, with bounded extraction covering varied documents.
tasks.still_hard: Obtaining lawful access, interpreting refusals and deciding whether records are sufficient remain difficult. Some records will still arrive late or on paper.
tasks.human_edge: Judging necessity, proportionality and the significance of missing or contradictory records.

ambition.what: A pre-review missing-records brief for legal counsel.

tasks.altitude: The legal assistant spends less time chasing and indexing, and more time resolving disputed or incomplete requests. They can reprioritise routine follow-ups within approved scope; counsel retains scope and disclosure decisions.

reach.role: insurance claims and policy processing clerk
reach.task: Assemble supporting records for a claim.
reach.learn: Evidence requirements, lawful request authority and how to distinguish missing records from unavailable records.

evidence.claim: BaseNeQXt supports legal case files and templates; this does not establish automated medical-record collection.
Health records contain special-category personal data under GDPR Article 9.
The Dutch data-protection authority documents a breach involving medical data entered into an AI chatbot.
In the Netherlands, statutory lawyer secrecy also binds employees and staff.
The proposed extraction checks, build ranges and remaining-time estimates require customer validation.

Routine reminders retain the approved recipient, scope and attachments; changes return for approval.
Confidential processing uses an approved environment with restricted access, retention and processing terms.
No general integration into external medical or employment record systems is assumed.

Handle refusals, conflicting records and unreadable scans.
Maintain request templates and reminder limits.
Maintain access, retention rules and extraction quality checks.
tasks.statement: Assist attorneys in collecting information such as employment, medical, and other records.

tasks.short: Attend legal meetings and proceedings, record notes, and prepare an accurate internal record.

steps.what: Assemble the agenda, matter documents and previous notes from {DOCS}.
Attend the meeting or proceeding and capture contemporaneous notes.
Turn raw notes into a structured draft with decisions, uncertainties and actions.

loop.input: Raw notes, meeting pack and an authorised transcript only when recording is permitted.
loop.output: Draft meeting record with source references, unresolved points and proposed action owners.
loop.check: The legal secretary checks names, dates, quotations and source support; unsupported conclusions remain flagged.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per meeting; incomplete or conflicting sources return to manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide structure, but fragmented notes need language interpretation to produce a readable record.

steps.what: Resolve uncertain wording and approve the record's legal meaning with the lawyer.
File the approved record and link its actions to the matter file.

tasks.design: A small generator assembles a meeting pack from {CALENDAR} and {DOCS}; a bounded drafting loop structures the secretary's notes using an approved template. The lawyer approves legal meaning before a flow files the record in {DOCS} and creates approved actions in {PROJECT}. Attendance remains human; optional transcription requires an authorised service, permitted recording and appropriate access controls.
tasks.previous_blocker: Attendance, selective note-taking and legal interpretation were bundled together. Confidential notes and inconsistent filing made preparation and cleanup difficult to standardise.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing permissions, document templates and workflow tools can support a small implementation. Bounded drafting can organise free text, while AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building the surrounding glue.
tasks.still_hard: Speakers may be unclear, wording may be disputed, and recording may be prohibited. GDPR applies, national rules govern proceedings and employee consultation, and internal notes cannot replace an official procedural record.
tasks.human_edge: Notice hesitation, sensitive disclosures and legally significant omissions, then ask the lawyer for clarification at the right moment.

ambition.what: A weekly unresolved legal commitments review across active matters.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less pack assembly and note cleanup, with attendance largely unchanged. The secretary can gain authority to request missing action owners and escalate overdue commitments; legal interpretation remains with the lawyer.

reach.task: Track commitments across legal matters and operational projects.
reach.learn: Action ownership, dependency tracking and escalation thresholds.
Version control, access restrictions and retention schedules.

evidence.claim: Meeting-note and minutes generation exists today; this supports drafting assistance, not legal accuracy.
iBabs Debrief offers transcripts, summaries and board minutes; this is adjacent evidence rather than a legal-proceedings case.
The UK departmental evaluation reported meeting-summary time savings and hallucinations, without evidence of higher productivity.
The proposed assembly, approval and filing workflow is an engineering estimate, not a documented legal deployment.
Dutch works-council rules can require consent for relevant employee data-processing or monitoring arrangements.

Maintain meeting templates, approval routes and action-owner mappings.
Handle failed filing and duplicate action creation.
Review access, retention and any authorised recording arrangements.
tasks.statement: Attend legal meetings, such as client interviews, hearings, or depositions, and take notes.

tasks.short: Draft, format and circulate office memos from lawyers’ instructions.

steps.what: Receive instructions and clarify the memo’s audience, purpose and required action.
Find supporting records and the current approved memo template.
Draft the memo and apply the required formatting.

loop.input: Memo brief, approved template and permission-checked source pack
loop.output: Memo draft with source references and marked gaps
loop.check: Validate required fields and source links; the assistant checks factual support, recipients and wording.
loop.stop: One draft and at most one revision against explicit corrections; incomplete or unsupported drafts return to manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle fixed notices, but narrative instructions require wording and synthesis. Invoke the loop only for those passages.

steps.what: Review the memo’s substance and approve its final wording and audience.
Circulate the approved version and save the distribution record.

tasks.design: A structured brief in the {WORKFLOW} retrieves approved sources and templates from the {DOCS}. A deterministic generator fills standard notices, while a bounded drafting loop handles narrative passages; lawyer approval unlocks distribution through the {EMAIL} and saves the approved version in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates covered formatting but could not turn varied instructions into clear prose. Source selection, version control and approval often depended on mailbox exchanges.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can produce a reviewable first version from supplied sources. AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of connecting templates, source records and approval states.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous instructions and legal implications still need clarification. Drafting may save little time when reviewers must substantially rewrite the result.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding what readers should do and detecting wording that changes a legal or organisational commitment.

ambition.what: Plain-language action briefs for non-legal managers

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends more time clarifying instructions and improving reader comprehension. They can choose approved formats and distribution timing within delegated limits; lawyers retain approval of substance.

reach.task: Translate approved office policy into practical staff instructions
reach.learn: Audience testing, policy implementation and accessible writing

tasks.short: Find relevant legislation and court decisions, verify sources, and prepare research notes for a lawyer.

steps.what: Clarify the legal issue, jurisdiction, relevant dates and research scope with the lawyer.
Form queries and search legal research databases in {OTHER}.

loop.input: Research brief, permitted database fields and an approved legal terminology list.
loop.output: Proposed queries, executed search results and a reproducible search log.
loop.check: Enforce jurisdiction and date filters, validate query syntax, and let the secretary inspect search coverage.
loop.stop: At most three query batches within a configured result cap; sparse results or scope changes return to the secretary.
loop.why_not_simpler: Saved searches cover repeat topics; new legal issues require translating free-text facts into alternative search terms.

steps.what: Read candidate legislation and decisions, checking relevance and current status.

loop.input: Retrieved source texts, available status metadata and research brief.
loop.output: A ranked shortlist with source passages, status flags and reasons for inclusion or exclusion.
loop.check: Resolve source identifiers, match quotations to retrieved text, and have the secretary inspect shortlisted authorities and exclusions.
loop.stop: One screening pass over the capped result set; missing texts, conflicting status or unclear holdings go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Metadata filters cannot establish whether a decision's facts and reasoning address the research question.

steps.what: Compile citations, relevant passages and open questions into a research note.
Verify citations and assess whether the authorities support the proposed legal use.
Save the reviewed note and source references in the matter file.

tasks.design: A structured request in {WORKFLOW} captures jurisdiction, dates and the legal question; bounded query drafting and source screening operate only on approved legal research databases in {OTHER}. Deterministic code builds a research note from checked citations and selected passages, then files the lawyer-reviewed version in {DOCS}. Source links and the search log remain attached so another person can reproduce the work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Legal relevance depends on language and context, while database licences and interfaces complicate retrieval. A formatted answer alone does not establish that sources exist, remain current or support the intended argument.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded language processing can propose search variants and screen retrieved text. Deterministic retrieval, citation checks and templates can handle the surrounding work without autonomous research.
tasks.still_hard: Negative research, conflicting authorities and current legal status require careful checking. Licensed database access may dominate cost; confidentiality, GDPR, EU AI Act duties and applicable national rules still need attention.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a missing line of authority, challenge a misleading factual analogy and know when the question needs a lawyer's interpretation.

ambition.what: A monthly legal-change brief for procurement managers on approved contract topics.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repetitive searching and formatting towards checking coverage and discussing uncertain findings. The secretary can gain authority to launch approved topic updates and request a wider search; advice and litigation choices remain with the lawyer.

reach.learn: Process mapping, impact assessment and clear separation of legal findings from business recommendations.

tasks.statement: Review legal publications and perform database searches to identify laws and court decisions relevant to pending cases.

tasks.short: Package search findings and obtain a lawyer’s approval before using them.

steps.what: Collect articles and search results relevant to the lawyer’s research request.
Check citations, jurisdiction, publication dates and source versions in the legal research service.
Select relevant passages and annotate how each source addresses the request.

loop.input: Research request and verified source texts
loop.output: Proposed relevance labels, exact excerpts and source locations
loop.check: Match excerpts exactly to source text; the assistant checks relevance, context and omitted qualifications.
loop.stop: One pass per source within the configured document limit; unreadable or oversized sources return to manual annotation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Metadata filters cannot establish whether a passage addresses a free-text legal question.

steps.what: Assemble findings, source copies and unresolved questions into a review packet.
Assess the findings and approve which sources may support the legal work.
Record the approval and share the approved packet with the matter team.

tasks.design: An adapter imports selected results from the legal research service in the {OTHER} into a permission-controlled source register in the {DOCS}. tasks.short: Complete legal, accident and application forms using matter records.

steps.what: Identify the required form, current version, jurisdiction and filing deadline.
Gather required facts and resolve missing information from the matter file.

loop.input: Approved form schema and matter records.
loop.output: Proposed field values with source references and explicit missing fields.
loop.check: Validate required fields, formats and cross-field consistency. A person verifies consequential values against their sources.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one validation retry per form; missing, conflicting or unsupported facts remain blank for a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: Some required facts appear only in narrative documents. Structured matter fields bypass the loop.

steps.what: Enter facts into the form and assemble required attachments.
Review factual accuracy, legal choices, declarations and attachment sufficiency.
Obtain required signature and submit the approved form through the designated channel.
Save the filed version and receipt, then update the matter status.

tasks.enabler_now: Schema-based generators and integrations are cheaper to build, while bounded extraction reduces rekeying from narrative records.
tasks.still_hard: Jurisdiction-specific interpretation, contested facts, declarations and inaccessible portals remain costly. A completed form is not necessarily a legally sufficient filing.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing legally appropriate answers and recognising when the available facts do not support a declaration.

tasks.short: Prepare client bills and route legal account expenses for approval and payment.

steps.what: Collect time entries, disbursements and agreed rates from the legal matter-management system.
Generate a draft client invoice with rates, tax treatment and matter references.
Review fees, disputed time, sensitive descriptions and proposed adjustments.
Issue the approved invoice and record the receivable.
Enter supplier invoices and assign matter, cost centre and expense codes.
Confirm the expense is valid and approve its allocation.
Include approved expenses in the payment batch and authorise bank release.

tasks.design: Connect time and disbursements in the legal matter-management category in {OTHER} to configured invoice generation in {ERP}, with fee exceptions routed through {WORKFLOW}. An approved client invoice is issued to the approved billing destination, while supplier invoices use existing capture, duplicate checks and coding rules in {ERP}. Budget approval and authorised payment release through {BANK} remain separate controls.
tasks.previous_blocker: Time records, fee agreements and finance records used different references. Exceptions and approvals travelled through mail, despite standard invoicing features already being available.
tasks.enabler_now: Configuration and small deterministic mappings can reuse existing billing and payable controls. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort needed to connect matter identifiers and reconcile rejected records.
tasks.still_hard: Fee disputes, confidential billing narratives, tax exceptions and changed bank details need attention. The assistant cannot infer commercial concessions or authorise payments without delegated authority.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding the client relationship, recognising inappropriate billing descriptions and challenging unsupported expenses.

ambition.what: Weekly review of unbilled disbursements before the billing cut-off.

tasks.altitude: The assistant moves from re-entry to resolving missing evidence and billing exceptions. They gain authority to correct routine coding within approved limits; fee concessions and payment authority remain with their existing owners.

tasks.short: Prepare, proofread and process legal documents under lawyer direction.

steps.what: Collect lawyer instructions, matter facts, supporting documents and the required procedural form.
Populate the approved template with parties, references, dates and standard wording.
Turn lawyer instructions into case-specific narrative and insert supplied legal references.

loop.input: Approved template, lawyer instructions, permitted matter facts and lawyer-supplied legal references.
loop.output: One draft with source-linked factual statements and explicit missing-information flags.
loop.check: Assistant checks source links and factual fidelity; lawyer verifies legal reasoning and citations before approval.
loop.stop: One draft per request, without autonomous searches or revisions; unsupported content is flagged for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Template fields handle standard wording. Case-specific narrative requires transforming free-text instructions into coherent prose.

steps.what: Proofread names, dates, numbering, cross-references, enclosures and formatting.
Review legal substance, verify authorities and approve the final document and intended filing.
Submit the approved document through the court portal and retain the submission receipt.

tasks.design: A generator joins approved matter data from the legal matter-management category in {OTHER} to controlled templates in {DOCS}, with deterministic checks for fields, numbering and enclosures. One bounded model pass drafts only the case-specific narrative from supplied instructions and sources, producing a source map and missing-information list. The lawyer approves legal substance and intended filing before the assistant submits through {GOV_PORTAL}; correspondence dispatch uses the separate approved-delivery workflow.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates could populate standard fields, but case-specific instructions and inconsistent source documents still required manual assembly. Procedural variation and costly legal errors limited unattended processing.
tasks.enabler_now: Template configuration and deterministic document checks already cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding makes small generators cheaper, while a bounded drafting pass can reduce transcription and rewriting.
tasks.still_hard: Correct facts do not establish a sound legal argument. Jurisdiction, current authorities, procedural deadlines and national filing rules need qualified review; model output can increase checking work.
tasks.human_edge: Interpreting the lawyer's intent, spotting omissions with legal consequences and recognising when standard wording misrepresents the matter.

tasks.short: Arrange lawyers’ travel, obtain approval and provide a usable itinerary.

Search the travel booking service for transport and accommodation options.

Approve the itinerary, spending limit and any policy exception.
Check current prices and terms, then purchase the approved travel.
Send the final itinerary, add calendar entries and forward the invoice to finance.

tasks.design: A travel request in the {WORKFLOW} draws appointment details from the {CALENDAR} and applies configured filters in the travel booking service in the {OTHER}. A deterministic generator builds the comparison and itinerary; after spend approval, the assistant confirms the purchase, and an integration distributes booking details through the {EMAIL}, {CALENDAR} and {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Traveller preferences and approval limits lived in messages. Changing fares, cancellation terms and fragmented booking interfaces made dependable purchasing automation expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured requests, existing travel filters and small itinerary generators cover much of the preparation. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of linking booking confirmations to calendars and invoice intake.
tasks.still_hard: Live prices, disruptions and cancellation conditions remain variable. Purchasing stays manual where the service lacks a dependable interface or the approved option has changed.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a workable journey around demanding appointments and resolving disruptions with the traveller.
